text:
Tara: Heads-up — hit an auth/retry + runtime error when bundling our webapp for Cloudflare Workers using the SDK ESM build. Works in node, fails only in Workers. Error: ReferenceError: require is not defined and Buffer is undefined.

Omar: Can you paste a minimal repro or the stack? Which SDK version + bundler?

Tara: SDK v1.2.3, esbuild target=browser, platform=neutral. Minimal stack snippet:
```
Uncaught ReferenceError: require is not defined
    at file:///workspace/.netlify/build/function.js:12:23
    at internalRequire (internal.js:45)
```
Also seeing polyfills pulling in node-libs, and retry code referencing setTimeout with a Node-style timer helper.

Jess (DevEx): CF Workers don't have Node globals (Buffer, process, stream). The ESM build is accidentally pulling a CJS auth transport that does `require('stream')`. Need an edge-specific build using fetch-only transports and no node core deps. Can you paste package.json exports?

Tara: snippet from package.json:
```json
{
  "main": "dist/index.cjs",
  "module": "dist/index.mjs",
  "exports": {
    ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" }
  }
}
```
Esbuild still pulls in a commonjs helper because of sourcemap/source references.

Mike: sourcemaps can pull original sources into the bundle and trigger CJS helpers. Quick mitigation: publish a separate dist/edge/index.mjs that intentionally avoids node shims and uses a fetch-based transport. Update exports to point browser/import to the edge file. Example exports idea:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "browser": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
  }
}
```
This tells bundlers to prefer the edge-friendly file in browser-like targets.

Jess (DevEx): Also add a top-level "types" pointing at the edge d.ts ("types": "dist/edge/index.d.ts"). Typescript tip: include lib: ["dom", "dom.iterable"] in tsconfig so lib defs for fetch/ReadableStream are available. Avoid depending on node types in the edge build.

Omar: For the auth/retry behavior specifically, make sure the SDK picks the fetch-based retry transport instead of node-fetch wrappers. Example usage that works in Workers:
```js
import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({
  transport: { kind: 'fetch' },
  auth: { apiKey: env.REDWOOD_API_KEY },
  retry: { maxRetries: 2, backoff: 'exponential' }
});
```
Switching to that removed the require/Buffer path for me.

Tara: Confirmed — swapping to the edge build + fetch transport removed the runtime errors. One remaining annoyance: sourcemaps still point at original TS files which makes CF logs noisy.

Jess (DevEx): Two choices: 1) disable sourcemaps for edge bundles (esbuild: "sourcemap: false") or 2) upload sourcemaps to your error tracker (Sentry) and configure worker source mapping. We're going to add a BUILD_EDGE.md with recommended esbuild flags and a small esbuild wrapper that forces platform=browser, target=es2020, sourcemap=false for the edge bundle.

devex-bot: Created ticket DE-487 "Edge ESM build: remove node core deps, add edge transport, docs + types" and assigned to @Mike.

Mike: I'll open a PR that adds dist/edge, updates package.json exports, and adds a GH Action job using Miniflare to smoke-test the worker bundle. Also planning a small test that runs the SDK in a Miniflare environment against our integration harness.

Tara: Thank you all — this unblock is huge. :thumbsup:

Jess (DevEx): Follow-ups: make sure our published package has an explicit "edge" entry in the README + examples showing the fetch transport and a tiny esbuild config block. I'll draft the README section this week.

Omar: Also - consider adding a lightweight runtime check that throws a helpful error if node-only transports are selected in edge environments (detect missing Buffer/process and surface a clear message). That will save folks debugging time.

Mike: good call. I'll add the check to the edge build and unit tests.

Tara: sending the quick patched bundle to staging now, will report back if anything else shows up.

Mike: awesome — thanks for catching and reporting.
